data: The French engine later licensed to India as Vikas — powered Ariane 1–4
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; ESA imagery.
The French engine that became India's workhorse

The Viking engine, developed by SEP in France for CNES and ESA, powered the first through fourth generations of the Ariane family from Ariane 1's inaugural launch on 24 December 1979. It burns nitrogen tetroxide and UH25 — a nitrogen-hydrazine blend — in a gas-generator cycle, a hypergolic propellant combination that trades efficiency for room-temperature storability and ignition simplicity. The Viking's most consequential second act came when ISRO licensed the design from France in the 1970s and developed it into the Vikas engine, which still flies on Indian launch vehicles today. One French engine design seeded two nations' access to space.
